title: Beyond the interface: Persistent Hopping Transport and Frequency Dispersion in Strong-inversion Cryogenic MOSFETs
authors: Keito Yoshinaga, Wataru Miyagi, Ryo Toyoshima, Munehiro Tada, Ken Uchida
abstract: Cryogenic complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (cryo-CMOS) technology is essential for quantum computing interfaces, which require precise modeling of dynamic device behavior. The output impedance of MOS field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) is frequency dependent, which has been conventionally attributed to extrinsic parasitics. Here, we report an intrinsic frequency dispersion in the channel impedance of cryogenic MOSFETs that persists deep into the strong-inversion region. Through a Cole-Cole analysis, we characterize this dispersion as a depressed semicircle in the impedance plane and attribute its behavior to variable-range hopping through band-tail localized states. Unlike conventional models where band-tail states are confined to the oxide interface, we demonstrate that in MOSFETs with high channel doping the band-tail states are induced by ionized impurities and distributed throughout the depletion region. Our paradigm accounts for frequency dispersion under strong inversion. This work demonstrates that ionized-impurities-induced hopping governs the dynamic response of cryo-MOSFETs channel impedance even when drift conduction dominates, offering critical insights for accurate small-signal modeling and high-frequency cryo-CMOS circuit design.
summary: This work investigates intrinsic frequency dispersion in MOSFETs operating at cryogenic temperatures. The authors demonstrate that this dispersion originates from variable-range hopping through band-tail states caused by ionized impurities distributed throughout the depletion region, not just at the oxide interface. This provides a critical correction for accurately modeling high-frequency behavior in cryo-CMOS circuits.
main_problem: To characterize intrinsic frequency dispersion in the channel impedance of cryogenic MOSFETs, particularly deep into the strong-inversion region.
main_result: The frequency dispersion is attributed to variable-range hopping through band-tail localized states induced by ionized impurities distributed throughout the depletion region, even when drift conduction dominates.
method: Impedance measurements using LCR meters and analysis via Cole–Cole (Nyquist) plots, combined with DC electrical characterization across varying temperatures and gate voltages.
model_or_system: The physical system is cryogenic complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (cryo-CMOS) MOSFETs. The model involves analyzing transport mechanisms in the presence of electrostatic disorder from ionized impurities within the semiconductor depletion region.
key_observables: Frequency dispersion characterized by a depressed semicircle in Cole–Cole plots; temperature dependence of conductance ($g_d \propto \exp(T/T_0)^{-1/3}$); extracted circuit parameters ($R_{DC}, R_{AC}, C_{AC}$).
important_parameters: Cryogenic temperatures (down to 4.2 K); strong-inversion regime; high channel doping levels.
main_assumptions: The frequency dispersion is governed by hopping conduction through impurity-induced band-tail states, which persists even when drift conduction dominates the DC current.
figures_summary: Figures show $	ext{I}_d-	ext{V}_g$ curves and Cole–Cole plots demonstrating the transition to depressed semicircles at low temperatures. Other figures detail the comparison between conventional interface-confined models and the proposed impurity-distributed model.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of intrinsic frequency dispersion in cryo-MOSFETs, presents measurements showing this dispersion via Cole-Cole plots, develops a theoretical framework attributing it to VRH through distributed band-tail states, and contrasts this finding with conventional interface-only models.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state electronics, the underlying physics—variable-range hopping in disordered potentials induced by impurities—is a canonical problem studied in condensed matter theory related to localization phenomena.
